entities.name: Lucius Aemilius Mamercinus Privernas
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lucius Aemilius Mamercinus Privernas, a distinguished Roman statesman of the mid-4th century BCE, served the burgeoning Roman Republic in multiple high offices during a critical period of its expansion and consolidation of power in central Italy. His career, spanning from at least 342 BCE to 316 BCE, saw him hold the consulship twice (341, 329 BCE), the critical role of Magister Equitum (342 BCE), and the extraordinary office of Dictator twice (335, 316 BCE), along with a term as Interrex (326 BCE). A scion of the influential Aemilia gens, his actions were instrumental in Rome's military and political maneuvering against the Latins, Samnites, and other Italic peoples, particularly during the Second Latin War and the early phases of the Samnite Wars, solidifying Roman hegemony over Latium and beyond.

During his first consulship in 341 BCE, Mamercinus Privernas, alongside his colleague Gaius Plautius Decianus, was primarily engaged in campaigns against the Samnites, securing victories that contributed to a peace treaty that year, albeit one that left the Latins vulnerable to Roman ambition. His dictatorship in 335 BCE saw him appoint Quintus Publilius Philo as Magister Equitum, and together they managed crucial military operations. Later, in his second consulship of 329 BCE, he led forces against the Privernates and Fundani, successfully capturing Privernum and initiating the process of its integration into Roman territory, a testament to Rome’s relentless policy of territorial absorption and subjugation.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Lucius Aemilius Mamercinus Privernas's extensive career in high Roman magistracies, including two consulships and two dictatorships, was crucial in expanding and consolidating Roman territorial control during the critical 4th century BCE, particularly against the Latins and Samnites. His actions directly contributed to Rome's emergence as the dominant power in central Italy.
